result:
I’d make it so **every decision that affects other people has to include their direct consent**—not just in obvious cases, but across everyday systems too (work, housing, healthcare, data, education, public policy).

It wouldn’t mean “everyone gets a veto on everything,” but it would mean people couldn’t be used as background variables. If your choice impacts my life, my agency would be built into the process.

In practice, that would look like:
- stronger consent and opt-in defaults for data and tracking  
- fairer power in workplaces (not “company rules” imposed on people)  
- transparent, understandable policies with meaningful opt-out/appeal paths  
- community control over things like local resources and development  
- real enforcement, not just “privacy terms” nobody reads  

If you want, tell me what kind of change you’re thinking about—social, political, technological, environmental—and I’ll try to match your vibe.
